headline: Anderson's Late Surge Powers Colorado Past Georgia 42-28
dek: Colorado evens its record at 1-1 while Georgia falls to 0-2 in the Eastern Southern cellar.
body: With 1:25 left and Colorado clinging to a 35-28 lead, Roger Anderson handed off to Benjamin Sweeney on third-and-short from the Georgia 16; Sweeney burst through the line for a 16-yard touchdown that pushed the margin to 42-28 and effectively sealed the game.

Georgia struck first on a 17-yard strike from TJ Giles to Colbie Young at the 10:00 mark of the first quarter, but Colorado answered 1:47 later when Anderson found Everett Payne for a 26-yard score. The Buffs took their first lead early in the second on a one-yard plunge by Mike Van Horne, only for Georgia to reel off two touchdowns — a 10-yard Giles-to-Marc Williams connection and a four-yard shovel to Jimmy Campbell — to lead 21-14 at halftime. Colorado leveled it at 21 on another Van Horne run midway through the third, then exploded for three fourth-quarter touchdowns: a short Payne catch, a 27-yard dart to Silas Bolden, and the decisive Sweeney run.

Anderson finished 24 of 38 for 350 yards and three touchdowns, lifting his season total to 662 yards and six scores — third in the PCFL — while Colorado's offense rolled up 462 yards against a Georgia defense allowing 472 per game, 17th in the league. Georgia's Giles threw for 254 yards and four scores but was intercepted once by Shilo Sanders, and the Bulldogs managed only 142 rushing yards to Colorado's 117 despite holding the ball for 33:38. The Buffs converted 50 percent of third downs and both fourth-down tries, and a 51-yard Anderson-to-Alton Mecum connection in the fourth quarter set up the go-ahead score.

The win moves Colorado to 1-1, keeps them second in the Western Central behind Michigan, and extends their winning streak to one; Georgia drops to 0-2, sits last in the Eastern Southern division behind leader LSU, and has lost two straight. Next week the Bulldogs travel to face Notre Dame (1-1) while Colorado returns home to host Boston College (0-2).
turningPoint: Q4 1:25 — Benjamin Sweeney's 16-yard touchdown run on third-and-short gave Colorado a 42-28 lead.
byTheNumbers: Anderson's 350 passing yards pushed his season total to 662, third in the PCFL behind only Geor MacIntyre's 725.
Georgia held a 33:38 to 26:22 time-of-possession edge but was outgained 462-393, highlighting Colorado's explosive efficiency.
Zero penalties for Colorado against one for Georgia; the clean sheet helped the Buffs sustain drives without self-inflicted setbacks.
Colorado converted 6 of 12 third downs (50%) and both fourth-down attempts, while Georgia went 7 of 15 on third down and 4 of 4 on fourth down.

unsungHero.name: Mike Van Horne
unsungHero.why: Scored two short-yardage touchdowns and churned out key carries on the game-clinching drive, providing the ground balance that let Anderson attack downfield.
